# Document Retention and Destruction Policy

**DRAFT, not adopted.** This draft is generated by policies/project.mjs from policies/register.json. It has no effect until the Board of Directors adopts it as the staged act below states; nothing here has been adopted, filed, posted or sent. It is not legal advice.

Standard models and authorities: Instructions for Form 990 Part VI line 14; 18 U.S.C. 1519; 26 U.S.C. 6001 and 26 CFR 1.6001-1; 26 U.S.C. 6104(d) and 26 CFR 301.6104(d)-1; IRS Publication 4221-PC; C.R.S. 7-136-101; Bylaws Article XI.

## Document Retention and Destruction Policy

**1. Purpose.** This policy identifies the record retention responsibilities of staff, volunteers, board members, and outsiders for maintaining and documenting the storage and destruction of the Corporation’s documents and records.

> Carries its authorities verbatim. Authority: Instructions for Form 990 (2025), Part VI, Section B, lines 13 and 14 (document retention and destruction policy); Instructions for Form 990 (2025), Part VI, Section B, lines 13 and 14 (books and records).

**2. Responsibilities.** The Secretary is custodian of the corporate records and keeps the minutes of the meetings of the Board of Directors. The Treasurer has charge and custody of and is responsible for all funds and securities of the Corporation and keeps its accounting records. Each director, officer, staff member, volunteer and outside party who holds a document or record of the Corporation shall retain it for the period the schedule in Section 4 states and shall document its storage and its destruction.

> Composed from its authorities. Authority: Bylaws 5.8; Bylaws 5.7; Bylaws 11.2; Instructions for Form 990 (2025), Part VI, Section B, lines 13 and 14 (document retention and destruction policy).

**3. Form of records.** The Corporation shall maintain its records in written or electronic form.

> Carries its authorities verbatim. Authority: Bylaws 11.3; C.R.S. 7-136-101.

**4. Retention schedule.** Each class of record is retained for the longest period any authority below states for it; a class for which no pinned authority states a period is retained until the Board of Directors adopts a period for it.

| Record | Retained | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Articles of incorporation and every amendment | Permanently | IRS Publication 4221-PC (Rev. 3-2018), Record Retention Periods, Permanent Records (Permanent Records); Bylaws 11.4 (11.4(a), a copy at the principal office); C.R.S. 7-136-101 ((5)(a), a copy at the principal office) |
| Bylaws and every amendment | Permanently | IRS Publication 4221-PC (Rev. 3-2018), Record Retention Periods, Permanent Records (Permanent Records); Bylaws 11.4 (11.4(b), a copy at the principal office); C.R.S. 7-136-101 ((5)(b), a copy at the principal office) |
| Minutes of Board and committee meetings, records of actions without a meeting, of committee actions on the Board's behalf, and of waivers of notice | Permanently | Bylaws 11.1 (11.1, permanent records); C.R.S. 7-136-101 ((1), permanent records); IRS Publication 4221-PC (Rev. 3-2018), Record Retention Periods, Permanent Records (Permanent Records, board minutes) |
| Application for recognition of exemption (Form 1023) with its supporting documents, and the IRS determination letter | Permanently | IRS Publication 4221-PC (Rev. 3-2018), Record Retention Periods, Permanent Records (Permanent Records); Bylaws 11.4 (11.4(e), a copy at the principal office); 26 CFR 301.6104(d)-1(a) ((a), available for public inspection) |
| Books of account | Permanently | 26 CFR 1.6001-1(c) ((c), permanent books of account or records) |
| Records that support an item of income or deduction on a return | 3 years; three years after the date the return is due or filed, whichever is later, and for as long as their contents may become material in the administration of any internal revenue law (Section 7) | IRS Publication 4221-PC (Rev. 3-2018), How Long Should Records be Kept? (period of the statute of limitations) (How Long Should Records be Kept?) |
| Annual information returns (Form 990 series) as filed, with schedules and attachments | 3 years; three years beginning on the date the return is required to be filed (with extensions) or is filed, whichever is later | 26 CFR 301.6104(d)-1(a) ((a), public inspection); IRS Publication 4221-PC (Rev. 3-2018), Public Inspection, Annual Information Return (Public Inspection); Bylaws 11.4 (11.4(d), Forms 990 for the last three years at the principal office) |
| Form 990-T as filed | 3 years; if the Corporation files Form 990-T: three years from the date it is required to be filed, including any extension | IRS Publication 4221-PC (Rev. 3-2018), Public Inspection, Form 990-T (Public Inspection, Form 990-T) |
| Financial statements | 3 years; statements for periods ending during the last three years | Bylaws 11.4 (11.4(d)); C.R.S. 7-136-101 ((5)(h)) |
| Employment tax records | 4 years; if the Corporation has employees: at least four years after filing the fourth quarter for the year | IRS Publication 4221-PC (Rev. 3-2018), Record Retention Periods, Employment Tax Records (Employment Tax Records) |
| List of the names and business or home addresses of the current directors and officers | While current; kept current | Bylaws 11.4 (11.4(c)); C.R.S. 7-136-101 ((5)(f)) |
| Most recent periodic report to the Secretary of State | While current; the most recent report | C.R.S. 7-136-101 ((5)(g)) |
| Written communications to members generally as members | 3 years; communications within the past three years | C.R.S. 7-136-101 ((5)(e)) |
| Conflict of interest annual statements and disclosures of interests (Conflict of Interest Policy Articles VI and IX) | No period stated: kept until the Board adopts one | none pinned (open claim) |
| Records of information reported under the Whistleblower Policy and of its handling | No period stated: kept until the Board adopts one | none pinned (open claim) |
| Contribution records and donor acknowledgments | No period stated: kept until the Board adopts one | none pinned (open claim) |

> Schedule. Authority: IRS Publication 4221-PC (Rev. 3-2018), How Long Should Records be Kept?; 26 U.S.C. 6001; 26 CFR 1.6001-1(c); Bylaws 11.1; C.R.S. 7-136-101.

**5. Records kept at the principal office.** The Corporation shall keep a copy of each record Section 11.4 of the Bylaws and C.R.S. 7-136-101(5) name at its principal office, for the period each states.

> Composed from its authorities. Authority: Bylaws 11.4; C.R.S. 7-136-101.

**6. Public inspection.** The Corporation shall make its application for tax exemption, and its annual information returns, available for public inspection as 26 U.S.C. 6104(d) and 26 CFR 301.6104(d)-1 require. Each annual information return shall be made available for a period of three years beginning on the date the return is required to be filed (determined with regard to any extension of time for filing) or is actually filed, whichever is later.

> Carries its authorities verbatim. Authority: 26 U.S.C. 6104(d); 26 CFR 301.6104(d)-1(a); IRS Publication 4221-PC (Rev. 3-2018), Public Inspection, Annual Information Return.

**7. Records material to the internal revenue laws.** The books and records 26 CFR 1.6001-1 requires shall be kept at all times available for inspection by authorized internal revenue officers or employees, and shall be retained so long as the contents thereof may become material in the administration of any internal revenue law, even after the period the schedule states.

> Carries its authorities verbatim. Authority: 26 CFR 1.6001-1(e); 26 U.S.C. 6001.

**8. Records needed for other purposes.** When records are no longer needed for tax purposes, the Corporation shall keep them until they are no longer needed for non-tax purposes.

> Carries its authorities verbatim. Authority: IRS Publication 4221-PC (Rev. 3-2018), Record Retention Periods, Records for Non-Tax Purposes.

**9. Suspension of destruction.** No document or record shall be altered, destroyed, mutilated, concealed, covered up or falsified with the intent to impede, obstruct, or influence the investigation or proper administration of any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the United States or any case filed under title 11, or in relation to or contemplation of any such matter or case. When the Corporation knows of such a matter or case, or of information reported under the Whistleblower Policy that concerns one, the Secretary shall suspend the destruction of every record that relates to it until the matter or case is closed.

> Carries its authorities verbatim. Authority: 18 U.S.C. 1519; Instructions for Form 990 (2025), Part VI, Section B, lines 13 and 14 (18 U.S.C. 1513(e) and 1519); Bylaws 5.8.

**10. Destruction.** When a record's retention period ends and no suspension under Section 9 and no need under Sections 7 or 8 applies, its custodian may destroy it, and shall document the destruction in the Corporation's records: the class of record, its period, the date and the method.

> Composed from its authorities. Authority: Instructions for Form 990 (2025), Part VI, Section B, lines 13 and 14 (document retention and destruction policy); Bylaws 11.3.

**11. Adoption.** The Board of Directors adopts this policy, and may amend it, by the act of a majority of Directors present at a meeting at which a quorum is present, or by written action under Section 4.12 of the Bylaws.

> Composed from its authorities. Authority: Bylaws 4.1; Bylaws 4.10; Bylaws 4.12.
